newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan money rates volatile on market operation.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan money rates volatile on market operation.

text.p: Pakistan's money market rates closed lower after opening sharply up on Thursday amid a special open market operation by the State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP), dealers said.
They said overnight rates were likely to open lower on Friday owing to high liquidity evident from the absence of any o discounting on Thursday.

"The special open market operation caused overnights to trade amid volatile conditions," a dealer at KASB & Co said. The market was unsure of the status of liquidity amid the operation, in which the SBP picked up an estimated 600 million rupees.
The overnights opened at 20 percent but most early trades were seen in the band of 17 and 20 percent, the dealer said.
"There was a temporary rise in rates but once again the lenders could not maintain the levels, and heavy activity was seen between the band of 13 percent and 15 percent."
Later rates fell to 12 percent and some deals were done at levels as low as 11 percent near close, the dealer said.
Uncertainty about the status of liquidity kept the term market almost inactive but offers for three-months were quoted at 16.10 percent, he said. -- Ovais Subhani 9221-5685192
